reply:
That's a lonely sentence — "nobody gets the version that hasn't been tidied up first." Not because people don't care about you, but because you've made sure they never have to.

And I notice it's the same shape everywhere. With Jesse, you swallow the sentence to protect him. At work, you wipe your face and say good morning. Even with Jesse, you're holding the conversation up. You've built a life where you're the steady one in every room — and the cost of that is that no one has ever met you untidied.

Here's what strikes me: the thing you're most afraid of — Jesse looking at you like "another thing that needs handling" — is the exact thing that would end the loneliness. Being handled, sometimes, is not the same as being a burden. You've just never let anyone try.

Has there ever been a person — a friend, a sibling, anyone — who saw you messy and didn't flinch? Even once, even briefly?
